[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/guiding-principle.md#ℹ-template-format-guidelines]

## ℹ️ Template Format Guidelines

This template uses an **enhanced dual-perspective approach** with a **business-first priority** to ensure principles serve both technical teams and business stakeholders:
page_texts.4:
[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/guiding-principle.md#-rationale-section]

### 💡 Rationale Section

- **Business-Focused Justification**: Explains why each principle is critical to organizational success, including direct business impact, strategic value, cost benefits, risk mitigation, and competitive advantages
- **Domain-Specific Benefits**: Highlights regulatory compliance, operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, revenue opportunities, and measurable business outcomes
- **Strategic Positioning**: Emphasizes long-term organizational benefits and competitive differentiation
page_texts.5:
[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/guiding-principle.md#-implementation-guidelines-structure]

### 📋 Implementation Guidelines Structure

- **Business Implementation**: Actionable guidance for business stakeholders, project managers, and decision makers (appears first)
- **Technical Implementation**: Specific guidance for development teams, architects, and technical implementers (follows business guidance)
page_texts.6:
[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/guiding-principle.md#-alignment-examples-structure]

### 🎯 Alignment Examples Structure

- **Business Perspective**: Business examples showing processes, decisions, and outcomes that demonstrate principle application (appears first)
- **Technical Perspective**: Concrete technical examples showing technologies, architectures, and development approaches (follows business context)

This **business-first dual approach** ensures principles are accessible to non-technical stakeholders while maintaining comprehensive technical guidance for implementers.

---

[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/guiding-principle.md#order-of-importance-optional] ## Order of Importance _(Optional)_ > **Use this section when**: Your domain has many principles (8+) or when stakeholders need clear prioritization guidance for decision-making and resource allocation. For domains with multiple competing principles, organize them by order of importance to guide decision-making when principles conflict or trade-offs must be made: | Tier | Priority Level | Principle | Description | | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------- | | 🔴 **Tier 1** | **[Category Name]**
_(Highest Importance)_ | **#1 [Principle Name]** | [Brief impact description] | | | | **#2 [Principle Name]** | [Brief impact description] | | | | **#3 [Principle Name]** | [Brief impact description] | | 🟡 **Tier 2** | **[Category Name]**
_(High Importance)_ | **#4 [Principle Name]** | [Brief impact description] | | | | **#5 [Principle Name]** | [Brief impact description] | | | | **#6 [Principle Name]** | [Brief impact description] | | 🟢 **Tier 3** | **[Category Name]**
_(Medium Importance)_ | **#7 [Principle Name]** | [Brief impact description] | | | | **#8 [Principle Name]** | [Brief impact description] | | 🔵 **Tier 4** | **[Category Name]**
_(Lower Importance)_ | **#9 [Principle Name]** | [Brief impact description] | **Tier Descriptions:** - **🔴 Tier 1**: [Description of highest priority principles - e.g., legal mandates, regulatory requirements, business-critical risks] - **🟡 Tier 2**: [Description of high priority principles - e.g., core business operations, strategic value delivery] - **🟢 Tier 3**: [Description of medium priority principles - e.g., long-term maintainability, operational efficiency] - **🔵 Tier 4**: [Description of lower priority principles - e.g., scalability benefits, performance optimization] > **Decision-Making Note**: When architectural decisions involve trade-offs between principles, prioritize higher-tier principles over lower-tier ones. For example, if implementing advanced optimization patterns (Tier 4) would compromise regulatory compliance requirements (Tier 1), prioritize the compliance requirement. All principles should be considered, but this hierarchy guides compromise decisions in real-world scenarios. ---
